passage:
Archaeologists studied old cooking tools and plant remains to understand what people ate long ago. A museum invited visitors to taste a modern version of an ancient dish.
The food was simple, made with grains, beans, and herbs. Some visitors liked it. Others found it plain.
The guide explained that food history shows trade, farming, class, and daily life. What people ate depended on what they could grow, buy, store, or cook.
A student realized that history can be tasted, not only read.
The ancient recipe did not make the past fully return, but it helped visitors imagine ordinary people sitting down to a meal thousands of years before them.
